notes_markdown:
**Heads-up before you update: this version changes how photos look in
Develop.** The tone maths behind Exposure, Highlights and white is new,
RAWs in the camera's look open in a refitted Vivid look, and the Color
Mix bands moved to the colours they're named for. Photos you've already
edited will look different when you open them in Develop — mostly in
their brightest tones — and Color Mix adjustments shift by a shade or
so. Photos you've already exported or saved to a server keep their saved
picture until you export or save them again (see Changed).

### New

- **Whites and Blacks sliders.** The Tone card gains Whites and Blacks
  after Shadows, for setting the two ends of the picture. Whites up
  stretches the brightest tones to white; down it brings back a RAW's
  detail above white. Blacks deepens or lifts the darkest tones. Neither
  ever swaps light and dark tones. Shift+double-click either one — or
  its part of the histogram — to set it to the clipping point. Photos
  whose sidecars carry Whites or Blacks from another editing tool now
  show them, and culler keeps them when it saves.
- **The histogram has five zones.** Blacks, Shadows, Exposure,
  Highlights and Whites, left to right: drag one to move its slider,
  double-click to reset it.
- **Hold Option to see exactly what clips.** While a highlight or shadow
  slider is in use, holding Option dims the photo and shows only the
  pixels that clip, each in the colour of the channels it lost — white
  means nothing is left. On a RAW, gold marks blown areas the sensor can
  still recover.
- **Right-click menus.** Right-click a photo — in the filmstrip, the
  Grid or the loupe — for a menu of what you can do to it: pick, reject,
  rate with stars, set a colour label, select, add to an album, open the
  batch panel on it, and in the loupe copy and paste settings, rotate,
  undo and export. On a photo that's part of your selection the menu
  acts on the whole selection. A right-click moves to the photo like a
  click and never changes the selection. Sources rows and saved filters
  have menus too — a row's menu offers exactly its keys, and deleting
  asks first, right in the menu. On a Mac, `Ctrl`+click works the same.
- **Select photos in the Grid by dragging a box.** Press on empty space
  between the thumbnails and drag across the photos you want: each one
  the box touches shows a check as you go, and letting go selects them
  (hold `Shift` or `Cmd` as you let go to add them to what's already
  selected). `Esc` cancels; nothing changes until you let go. Drag to the
  top or bottom edge and the grid scrolls on. And the tags on a photo
  are buttons now: click `[moment 3/8]` to survey the moment, the
  filmstrip's `×4` or `STACK · 4 photos` to step into a stack, `[stack]`
  to step back out.
- **See how much is clipping while you adjust.** While you move
  Exposure, Highlights, Shadows, Curve highlights or Curve shadows —
  dragging, scrolling over the slider, or dragging in the histogram — the
  bottom right of the histogram reads `clipped 0.8 %`: how much of the
  photo that end blows out or crushes, counted the way the corner
  triangles count it. It turns amber past 0.5 %.
- **Fine and coarse control on every develop slider.** Hold `Option`
  while you drag a slider or drag in the histogram and it moves a tenth
  as far; hold `Shift` and it moves four times as far — and with the
  scroll wheel or the step keys they pick a fine or a big step. The
  slider's knob shrinks or grows and a `fine` / `coarse` caption appears
  beside its value while the key is down.
- **Steer a develop slider from the keyboard.** Let go of a drag, click a
  slider's track or value, or press `[` / `]`, and that slider is aimed —
  its row lights up. Then `-` and `=` step it in its own units (Exposure
  0.10 EV, the other sliders 5; hold `Option` for the finest step, `Shift`
  for a big one), `Enter` types a value, `Backspace` resets it and `Esc`
  lets go. With nothing aimed, `=` and `-` step Exposure. The aim stays
  while you move from photo to photo, so you can nudge each frame of a
  series in turn.
- **Option-click a develop section's header to see only that section.**
  Option-click Tone, Color, Color Mix or Curve & Effects and that section
  opens while the other three fold away. A plain click still opens or
  closes just the one.

### Changed

- **RAWs in the Vivid look open much closer to the camera's own
  picture — this changes how RAW photos look.** The Vivid look now
  carries the camera's tone shape: shadows are no longer lifted and
  milky, the bright midtones no longer sit dull, and colours are closer
  to the camera's while grey cloud and mist stay grey. Measured against
  the camera's JPEGs on 24 test photos, every one came out closer.
  Untouched RAWs and RAWs edited on the camera look both open in the new
  look (their brightness refits once, automatically); photos already
  exported or saved to a server keep their saved picture until you save
  them again.
- **Color Mix bands now move the colour they're named for — this changes
  how existing Color Mix edits look.** Each band is centred on its
  colour as you see it: Yellow moves yellows (it used to leave a typical
  yellow untouched while Orange moved it), skin sits in Orange, and
  Hue turns a colour by the same visible amount whatever its brightness.
  Photos you've already adjusted in Color Mix will look different when
  you open them in Develop — usually only slightly: the adjusted colours
  shift by a shade or so, rarely more.
- **Saturation −100 is black and white on every photo.** On a RAW
  opening in the camera's look, Saturation now scales the look's own
  colour instead of adding to it, so −100 is fully black and white and
  every step of the slider — all the way to +100 — changes the picture.
- **Highlights no longer turns blown areas grey or leaves halos.**
  Pulling Highlights down compresses the bright tones below white and
  leaves white itself alone, so a blown sky or window stays white instead
  of going flat grey, light and dark tones never swap places even at −100,
  and there are no more dark rims round clouds. Strong pulls are a little
  gentler than before; photos you've edited with Highlights near either
  end will look slightly different.
- **White stays white, and pushed highlights no longer clip — this
  changes how existing edits look.** An untouched photo's white now
  renders at full white (it used to stop just short), raising Exposure
  rolls the brightest tones smoothly into white instead of flattening
  them, and colours keep their hue as they brighten. On a RAW, pulling
  Highlights down now brings back detail the sensor kept above white.
  **Photos you've already edited will look different when you open them
  in Develop**: anything pushed more than about one stop brighter keeps
  more highlight detail and reads slightly darker in the bright midtones,
  and every edited photo's whites move a few levels up. A RAW following
  the camera's look refits its brightness once, automatically. Photos
  already exported or saved to a server keep their saved picture until
  you export or save them again. The clipping warnings (`W`) now mark
  exactly display level 250 and up.
- **Hold `W` or `\` to peek.** A quick tap still turns the clipping
  warnings or before / after on and off. Holding the key now shows it
  only while you hold it — or, when it was on, hides it — and letting go
  puts it back.
- **Sliders you can read at a glance.** Every slider shows its track,
  with a small tick where a double-click returns it; once you move it, a
  fill grows from that tick to the value and a knob marks the spot.
  Values say which way they went and in what unit (`+15`, `−8`,
  `+0.67 EV`), and hovering one draws a field around it — click and type
  an exact number.
- **Scrolling over the develop panel scrolls it.** The scroll wheel now
  edits only the slider you've aimed (or any slider while you hold
  `Option`), so a swipe on your way down to Color Mix no longer moves the
  slider it passes over. Each notch is a finer step than before — 0.05 EV,
  or 2 on the other sliders.
- **A slimmer foot to the develop panel.** The line at the bottom now
  changes with what you're doing — while you drag a slider it lists the
  keys that steer it — and the sliders get back the room the old caption
  under the buttons took (it was cut off at the window's edge anyway).
- **Every develop slider has its own name.** The tone curve's four
  sliders are now Curve highlights, Curve lights, Curve darks and Curve
  shadows, so they no longer read as Tone's Highlights and Shadows, and
  the Color Mix rows name their colour — Orange hue, Orange saturation,
  Orange luminance.
- **Settings → RAW files → RAW opens in.** Choose whether a RAW you
  haven't edited opens in your camera's look (the default) or as the
  flat RAW. Photos you've already edited keep their look.
- **RAWs from any camera open at their JPEG's brightness.** A RAW from a
  camera culler has no look for used to open about a stop darker than its
  JPEG; it now opens matched to the JPEG's exposure (the picker reads
  **Camera exposure**), with contrast and colour still flat.
- **Stepping through RAWs in the develop panel is quicker.** The photos
  either side of the one you're on are prepared in the background, so
  the next RAW lands on its camera look straight away, and a photo you've
  already left stops being refined.
- **Auto works on top of the camera's look.** On a RAW in its camera
  look, `Shift+A` and the Auto button now tune the tone measured on that
  look and keep it — instead of only switching back to the look. Use
  **Camera look (default)** in the look picker to get back to the look.
- **The look picker says when you're on the camera's look.** It reads
  **Vivid · camera** while a RAW shows its camera look, and the list
  starts with **Camera look (default)** to get back to it.
- **Undo takes back one stretch of work at a time.** Several tweaks to
  the same slider used to undo all at once, however far apart you made
  them. Now one undo step ends when you pause for 8 seconds, move to
  another control, go to another photo, or quit — so a nudge you made a
  minute later undoes on its own. Reset, Auto, a look, a paste and a
  snapshot restore are always one step each, even back to back.

### Fixed

- **A slider you scroll is saved on its own photo.** Scrolling a develop
  slider and stepping to the next photo straight away used to leave the
  edit unsaved, and could nudge the next photo instead. The edit is now
  written to the photo you made it on — also when you close the panel,
  open another source or quit right after.
- **Match no longer wrecks a series shot at different exposures.** In a
  Match series session, pressing **Match** on a frame shot brighter or
  darker than the reference used to push Contrast, Highlights and
  Shadows to their limits and overshoot the exposure — the "it messes up
  the whole series" result. A frame that differs only in exposure now
  gets exposure alone, one that differs only in contrast gets contrast,
  and a frame whose darkest or brightest parts really changed is still
  only nudged — never by more than the difference itself, and never
  chasing a part that is pure black or blown white.
- **The histogram shows where a RAW's highlights really are.** With the
  camera's look on, the brightest parts of a RAW used to pile up in one
  false spike well short of white, and the curve over the histogram went
  flat across its top, while the picture kept all that detail; both now
  follow the picture. An untouched photo's histogram matches the screen
  too, so the smallest exposure nudge no longer makes it jump. And the
  clipping triangles in the histogram's corners ignore a few bright
  glints: they light when a real part of the photo — at least one pixel
  in 2,000 — reaches the level the `W` clipping overlay paints.
- **Match series shows RAWs in their camera look.** Inside a series
  session RAW photos used to drop back to the flat RAW; each now keeps
  its camera look, and Done saves the changed photos with it.
- **A RAW without a camera JPEG exports in the camera's look.** Pressing
  `J` on an untouched lone RAW used to render it flat, even though the
  develop panel showed it in the camera's look; it now exports the
  picture you see.
- **Dragging with the right mouse button no longer picks up the photo**
  (or pans a zoomed one) — only the left button drags. The previous and
  next arrows at the photo's edges no longer swallow a right-click.
- **Undo survives a server library that's still loading.** Editing a photo
  while a large Immich library was still streaming in used to drop that
  photo's undo history and snapshots the moment loading finished (the edit
  itself was kept). They stay now.
- **Opening a server source again keeps your saved edit history.**
  Refreshing an Immich source, or coming back to it from another source,
  used to bring back the photos you had already looked at without the
  undo history and snapshots you saved with `J` — and a photo with a saved
  snapshot then counted as unsaved — until culler restarted. They come
  back now, as they do at launch.
- **The sources panel's folder check no longer goes missing.** Closing the
  panel before its quick "is this folder still there?" check finished left
  an unplugged drive's folder unmarked until the panel opened again; the
  mark now lands either way.
- **Develop sliders are more precise.** A quick, small drag used to lose
  its first few points of travel, so a nudge moved a slider much less than
  your hand did; every point counts now. Double-clicking a slider's track
  resets it on every develop slider, as it always should have (most of
  them ignored it). And scrolling over the RAW Temperature slider now
  moves by the same share of its scale wherever it sits, instead of a
  big jump in warm light and a tiny one in cool.
